picks.title: Developers, not doctors, should be held accountable for generative AI medical devices, providers say
picks.excerpt: Provider groups are lobbying the FDA to make tech companies responsible for the safety and performance of generative AI-backed medical devices, arguing makers are best equipped to evaluate them.
picks.rationale: Covers the comments provider groups filed with the FDA's consultation on generative-AI medical devices, centred on who carries liability. That reaches regulators directly. It is the single kept item from a 5-article cluster on the same consultation.

picks.title: Sentara Health deploys new AI case management tool co-developed with Regard
picks.excerpt: Sentara Health rolled out an AI case-management tool built with Regard that lets case managers query charts in plain language for discharge planning; it plans to expand into acute and ambulatory care, projecting ~90,000 hours saved.
picks.rationale: A health system rolled out a plain-language chart-query tool for discharge-planning case managers, with a projected 90,000 hours saved. Neither Sentara nor Regard appears in the 30-day history.

picks.title: “목 찍다 놓친 폐암, AI가 잡아낸다” 의료영상 ‘기회검진’ 새 지평
picks.excerpt: 코어라인소프트의 흉부 CT 폐결절 AI 'AVIEW LCS'로 목 CT 판독에서 놓치기 쉬운 초기 폐암 병변을 검출한 연구가 Korean Journal of Radiology에 실렸다. 8만1794명 추적에서 폐암 확진자 123명의 과거 목 CT에 병변이 이미 찍혀 있었다.
picks.rationale: A Korean Journal of Radiology study that followed 81,794 people and found lung cancers on earlier neck CTs using AI-assisted opportunistic screening. The full URL (idxno=3014596) is new. The 10-10 Coreline card covered Japanese society certification, which is a different event.

picks.title: LLMs mostly avoid unnecessary care in Choosing Wisely tests
picks.excerpt: In an Annals of Internal Medicine study, LLMs recommended potentially unnecessary care in about 5% of Choosing Wisely scenarios, but over 40% of responses recommended thyroid ultrasound for small incidental nodules.
picks.rationale: An Annals of Internal Medicine study testing whether LLMs recommend low-value care. Its specific failure mode (thyroid ultrasound for small nodules) is something clinicians can act on. It is a different study from the 10-17 NEJM AI cost-of-care card.

picks.title: CT tool may detect pulmonary fibrosis progression more than 2 years sooner
picks.excerpt: Brainomix's FDA-cleared AI quantitative CT tool e-Lung flagged pulmonary fibrosis progression an average of 16 months (up to 28) before clinical diagnosis in 509 patients across three U.S. centers.
picks.rationale: A three-center study of 509 patients in which Brainomix's FDA-cleared e-Lung flagged pulmonary fibrosis progression a mean 16 months early. No fibrosis or Brainomix story appears in the history. The tagged 10-22 match is a pulmonary embolism study, a different disease and product.
